title: Maryland Higher Education secretary leaving after three years in job
summary: Maryland Higher Education Secretary Sanjay Rai is stepping down Friday, his last day leading the agency that oversees statewide policies on public and private colleges and universities.
content:
by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters March 25, 2026

by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters March 25, 2026

Maryland Higher Education Secretary Sanjay Rai is stepping down Friday, his last day leading the agency that oversees statewide policies on public and private colleges and universities.

Gov. Wes Moore (D), who appointed Rai as acting secretary in April 2023, announced Rai’s departure Tuesday. Rai was officially sworn in, without the “acting” title on May 1, 2024.

“Under his leadership, Maryland has opened new pathways for students to learn, grow, and succeed,” Moore said in his statement. “We are grateful for his service and will continue building on that progress to ensure every Marylander has access to a world-class education and a pathway to work, wages, and wealth.”

Rai said in a statement he was “proud of the work done to expand opportunity and strengthen workforce-aligned pathways for Maryland students.”

Deputy Secretary Elena Quiroz-Livanis, who has been at the agency since November 2024, will take over for Rai while a search is conducted for his replacement.

Just a few months into Rai’s tenure leading the agency known as MHEC, its board of commissioners voted in June 2023 to let Towson University create a business analytics doctoral program. Morgan State University President David Wilson said at the time it was similar to his school’s doctoral business administration program.

Program duplication was at the center of legislation approved two years earlier that authorized a $577 million settlement to end a 14-year-old lawsuit against the state, charging that it had provided more resources to white institutions. The suit also said the state allowed duplication of programs at the state’s four historically Black colleges and univerisities — Morgan State, Bowie State University, Coppin State University and the University of Maryland, Eastern Shore.

The General Assembly that year established the Program Review Process Advisory Council, which went into effect in July 2024, to help assess the review process for new higher education programs and prevent duplication of programs.

On Monday, Senate Bill 983 sponsored by Sen. Cory McCray (D-Baltimore City), was unanimously approved. It calls on the council to study and make recommendations on possible program duplication for “certain new undergraduate programs.” Program assessments are currently only done for graduate-level programs.

The bill would require the council to submit a report by Dec. 31 to the Senate Education, Energy and the Environment and the House Appropriations committees.

A House version sponsored by Del. Mellisa Wells (D-Baltimore City) was sent to House Rules and Executive Nominations Committee last month and dereferred ferred to the Appropriations Committee on March 16.
